subject: POC playbook & exec readout — Aurora Medical (next steps)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Diane Cole <diane@aurora-med.com>, Patrick O'Neill <patrick.oneill@aurora-med.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC playbook & exec readout — Aurora Medical (next steps)

Hi Diane / Patrick,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the clarity on what success looks like. I wanted to capture the follow-ups and propose a concise plan so we can move the POC forward this week. Attached: aurora_poc_playbook_v1.pdf (POC runbook) and redwood_sow_draft.docx (SOW - redlines welcome).

High-level recap & proposed approach:
- Primary objective: validate Redwood inference reduces average inference cost per query by >=35% while meeting 95th pct latency < 300ms for your 4k token clinical note workload.
- Key success metrics (please confirm):
  - Accuracy: model-level parity with current baseline on the clinical extraction task (F1 within 3 pts)
  - Latency: 95th percentile under 300ms for 1x steady-state concurrency
  - Cost: token-level cost reduction >= 35% vs current provider
- Scope & owners:
  - Data/sample set: Patrick to share 250 de-identified sample notes by Fri 8/21
  - Integration: lightweight API pass-through (no PHI in transit) — Redwood to provide test endpoints
  - Security artifacts: we can share SOC/pen-test summary; procurement will likely request more — see attachments.

Timeline (proposed compressed 4-week trial):
1) Week 0 (next 3 business days): kickoff + infra setup + sample ingestion
2) Week 1: baseline run + tuning (batching, quantization profile)
3) Week 2: evaluation against success prompts + quality check
4) Week 3: stabilization and readout prep
5) Week 4: exec readout & decision (go/no-go)

Proposed exec readout window: Sep 7–11; we recommend a 30–45 minute slot with Product + Exec Sponsor (Carlos) to present results and recommended next step.

Asks from you: please confirm the success metrics above, the list of internal reviewers (Carlos for exec), and confirm whether procurement prefers an SOW + PO or DocuSign flow.

If that looks good I’ll loop in CS and Solutions to lock owners and get the kickoff on calendar.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: aurora_poc_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 128KB); redwood_sow_draft.docx (DOCX, 34KB)
From: Diane Cole <diane@aurora-med.com>

Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 12:15:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: POC playbook & exec readout — Aurora Medical (next steps)

Aditya, thanks for the summary and the materials — very helpful. Quick confirmation/edits from our side: 

- Metrics: the accuracy requirement is correct but we’d prefer F1 within 2 pts, not 3. Latency target is fine. Cost target is a good goal but procurement will want estimates broken down by request type.
- Stakeholders: Diane (PM), Patrick (Engineering lead), Carlos (VP Product) — Carlos will take the exec slot if results look strong.
- Data: Patrick can deliver the 250 de-identified notes by EOD Friday 8/21. We will not be sending any PHI.
- Timeline: we’d be excited to try to compress to 4 weeks if Redwood can commit to prioritized support during tuning; otherwise 5 weeks is acceptable.
- Procurement: prefer SOW + PO. Our procurement lead will request SOC 2 Type II summary and an evidence checklist — can your team provide a short packet for procurement review?

Next steps from our side: Patrick to send samples; I will introduce our procurement contact once we get a draft SOW. Please confirm kickoff time windows.

— Diane
Diane Cole
Senior Product Manager, Aurora Medical

Subject: Re: Fwd: POC playbook & exec readout — Aurora Medical (next steps)

Thanks — happy to own the SE side. Quick tech notes after reviewing their workload and our playbook: 

- Data/ingest: we’ll run a small private test endpoint and ask for the 250 samples in JSONL; we’ll provide a script to sanitize and validate schema.
- Perf tuning: start with the 8-bit quantized profile (Q4_K_M) and continuous batching; if latency spikes on long notes we’ll fallback to mixed-precision optimized kernels.
- Sampling: we’ll mirror Aurora’s evaluation prompts. Priyom to run baseline within 48 hours of ingest and share a perf+quality snapshot.
- Risks: if they hit heavy concurrency (>= 8 concurrent long-run requests) we’ll need dedicated capacity or burst capacity enabled — call this out to the customer in kickoff.

I’ll prepare a short internal checklist for the 48-hour baseline run and upload to the shared Drive.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Diane / Patrick / Carlos — great to align. Confirming next steps and schedule so everyone has a single source of truth: 

- Kickoff: Tue 8/24 @ 10:00am PT (30m) — agenda: intro, sample handoff, access, initial baseline plan. Attendees: Patrick, Diane, Priyom, Marissa, Aditya.
- Baseline: Priyom will run 48-hour baseline after sample ingestion (target by Fri 8/28).
- POC window: compressed 4-week cadence from 8/24–9/18.
- Exec readout: Thu 9/9 @ 10:00am PT (30–45m) — expected attendees: Carlos (Aurora VP), Diane (PM), Patrick (Eng), Redwood exec + SE + CS. Decision ask: go/no-go on pilot/contract.
- Contract path: SOW (attached) -> Aurora PO. Diane, if procurement prefers, we’ll also generate a DocuSign copy after legal review.

Decision criteria at readout (explicitly):
1) Accuracy: meets customer threshold (F1 within 2 pts)
2) Latency: 95th pct < 300ms for target concurrency
3) Cost reduction: >= 35% (or clear economic case with caveats)
4) Ops: smooth integration, no major security blockers from procurement packet

Attachments included again: aurora_poc_playbook_v1.pdf; redwood_sow_draft.docx

Please accept the invites; we’ll drop a short procurement packet to Diane’s procurement contact after you introduce them. Looking forward to kickoff.

Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
